hints.geo.volume.prism: Volume = length × width × height: the cubes that fit inside.
hints.geo.volume.cylinder: Cylinder: π × radius² × height. Cone: one third of that.
hints.geo.volume: Box: l × w × h. Cylinder: πr²h. Cone: ⅓πr²h.

misconceptionMessages.geo.volume-added: Volume multiplies: length × width × height (and the radius is squared for a cylinder).
misconceptionMessages.geo.volume-surface: That's the surface (the faces). Volume is the space inside: length × width × height.
misconceptionMessages.geo.cone-no-third: A cone holds one third of the cylinder around it: multiply by ⅓.

sections.title: Volume of a box
sections.objective: Find the volume of rectangular prisms.
explain: Volume counts the unit cubes that fill a shape.
One layer on the bottom has length × width cubes; there are height layers.
sections.key: Volume of a box = length × width × height.

sections.title: Cylinders and cones
sections.objective: Find the volume of cylinders and cones, in terms of π.
explain: A cylinder is a stack of circles: the area of the circle times the height.
A cone fits inside a cylinder three times.

steps: The circle on the bottom: π × 3 × 3 = 9π.
So V = 45π in³. A cone this size would hold 15π in³.

sections.key: Cylinder: π × radius² × height. Cone: ⅓ × π × radius² × height.

sections.title: Putting it together
